_check.5: 1.1 · From activity to progress | Are we
_check.11: 2.2 · Four consequences of weak review d

5.label: Finished or settled
5.text: Many costly strategic decisions are made quietly mid-execution, when the team decides that what has been done is probably enough. Audit the exits: where exactly did we decide to stop, and why? The gap between results and potential often sits at that point.

5.label: Understanding and action
5.text: A culture that rewards understanding without requiring corresponding action trains people to be articulate more than effective. Check whether people acted on what they understood.

6.label: 02 · Establishes Accountability
6.text: Strategic completion requires tracking every component of the declared goal, including the parts that bring no visible victory. Record what has been accomplished as evidence that commitments are being kept.

6.label: Upstream conditions
6.text: Outcomes are shaped long before they become visible. Look past final performance indicators to the upstream conditions shaping decisions: information flows, incentives, norms, routines and dominant voices. Use this with 03 · Enables Learning.

7.label: Restore · renewed conviction
7.text: Stalled work needs renewed conviction as well as renewed activity. New deadlines alone achieve little; restore the purpose, authority and significance of the work so people understand why it must continue.

7.label: A recovery pathway in advance
7.text: The leader who designs the recovery pathway before a failure happens is doing a higher quality of work. Name one plausible failure and check whether a clear, understood recovery pathway exists. If it does not, build one.

8.label: Cannot or will not
8.text: Leaders must distinguish between team members who cannot perform and those who will not. The interventions differ: inability needs development and unwillingness needs accountability.

8.label: Simple causality
8.text: Avoid assuming that every negative outcome proves individual failure, or that every positive outcome proves sound practice. Use this with “Misfit or structural constraint”.

8.label: Specific accountability
8.text: Accountability works when it is specific and behaviour-based. Vague, general assessments of character produce no specific correction.

10.label: After visible success
10.text: Sustaining results often means returning to uncomfortable issues people assumed were resolved. Monitor whether commitments remain alive in actual behaviour; previous agreement does not guarantee continued delivery.

10.label: Analysis as delay
10.text: Requesting more evidence can be a substitute for acting on the evidence already available, and perpetual analysis often protects people from accountability for a decision. Where the evidence is sufficient, set a deadline and decide.

11.label: 01 · Early Warning Signals Are Missed
11.text: A strategy without an early warning system, a way to detect drift before collapse, is operating blind.

11.label: Deferred warnings
11.text: Most organisational decline accumulates through small warnings that everyone could see and no one acted on. Take the risk that has been deferred because it is not yet urgent and put a decision date against it before the deferral becomes the decision.

11.label: 03 · Loss of Organisational Learning
11.text: Reviews create little value when lessons remain conversational. Insight must alter decisions, controls, resource allocation and expected behaviour, or recurring problems keep being treated as isolated events.

12.label: Progress Confirmation
12.text: Teams that move from task to task without acknowledging progress build a culture where people feel invisible. Affirmation is structural.

12.label: Early Warning
12.text: Read a difficult moment accurately, naming it honestly without catastrophising it. The leader who treats every disruption as terminal loses the confidence of the people around them.

12.label: Significant Gap
12.text: Underperforming initiatives often receive an open-ended reprieve that no one revisits. Extensions should come with a defined window and concrete intervention, so that patience with a struggling effort does not become a permanent subsidy of failure.

14.label: Gap 02 · Evidence Quality
14.text: The most corrosive pattern is the gap between advertised and actual performance: dashboards that look green and reports that signal health with no results underneath. Make it safer to disclose a thin harvest than to perform a false one.

14.label: Gap 04 · Learning Suppression
14.text: Formal systems can exist while actual behaviour contradicts their purpose. Strategic reviews should examine lived practice alongside formal compliance.

16.label: Interdependence
16.text: Healthy organisations create conditions in which differentiated strengths work together. The test of collective culture: when one part suffers, others respond; when one succeeds, others celebrate. Indifference and internal envy both weaken collective performance.

18.label: Reviewing a win
18.text: When results are strong, leaders tend to credit their own judgement; when results are weak, they credit conditions. When reviewing a win, name the conditions, the inherited groundwork and the people whose work made it possible before naming your own decisions.

20.label: A shared signal system
20.text: Organisations that rely on leaders to communicate every directional shift in person are bottlenecked by access to those leaders. A shared, reliable signal system allows consistent coordination without constant individual instruction. Use this with “This board is where we make the system visible”.

21.label: What does this require of me?
21.text: The leader who receives honest feedback about a genuine problem and responds with honesty before justification, and action before communication, creates the conditions for real leadership. Use this to brief the CXO role.

21.label: Correction with a pathway back
21.text: Accountability without a pathway back becomes punishment. Correct firmly where necessary, and deliberately restore trust, contribution and dignity when change is evident.

22.label: 02 · Diagnosis
22.text: Leaders who either conceal failure or weaponise it prevent learning. Mature accountability names what went wrong, understands why it happened and moves people toward responsible change.

22.label: Intent and outcome
22.text: Holding people accountable for outcomes without considering intent produces a culture of blame. Intent matters.
